title: Telemetry-aware playbook scorer and staged auto-remediation framework
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds an automated playbook scoring engine that surface coverage gaps, estimated execution cost, and proposes gated staged-remediations with safe undo steps. Includes a GitHub Action check and a lightweight CLI to run scores locally.
description:
Context and motivation: On-call responders often see runbooks/playbooks that either assume telemetry that doesn't exist for the service, or include remediation steps that are costly or irreversible. This PR introduces a telemetry-aware playbook scoring engine plus a small staged auto-remediation framework to make playbooks safer and easier to evaluate (ENG-4521). The change focuses on three user problems: 1) quickly surface gaps between a playbook's assumptions and the telemetry actually available; 2) estimate the operational cost/risk of executing each step; 3) provide a gated staged-remediation runner that enforces safety checks and provides automated undo suggestions.

What this PR does (summary): - Adds a new playbook-scoring service under incident-bot/services/playbook_scoreer that computes a 0-100 score per playbook based on telemetry coverage, action risk, average execution cost (time/queries/calls), and a confidence metric when telemetry is incomplete. - Introduces a small staged remediation runner (incident-bot/runner/staged_runner) that executes playbook steps in discrete stages with preflight checks, simulated dry-run capability, and automatic undo-step registration when a step is annotated with "undo:" metadata. - Adds a git-hook / GitHub Action (ci/playbook_score_check.yml) which runs the scorer on any modified playbook YAML in PRs and blocks merges below a configurable threshold. - Includes a tiny CLI (bin/ib-playbook-score) for on-call engineers to locally score and simulate playbooks against a target environment (supports --dry-run and --simulate-cost flags). - Adds lightweight schema extensions to playbooks to declare telemetry expectations and cost hints (docs/playbook_schema.md).

Implementation notes: - Scorer uses a three-part signal: telemetry_presence, step_risk_model, and historical_execution_stats. Telemetry presence is computed by matching required metrics/logs/traces declared in the playbook against the telemetry index service (a contributed adapter; not changing the core telemetry index). Step risk leverages a small rule set mapping actions (restart, rollback, db-migrate, toggle-feature) to risk buckets; teams can extend via playbook metadata. Historical stats are optional and used only when present to improve cost estimates. - Staged runner enforces timeouts per stage and records a reversible action list when playbook authors provide undo instructions. The runner exposes a JSON-serializable execution trace that can be attached to incidents for postmortem and cost accounting. - The GitHub Action executes the scorer inside a PyPI-packaged wheel we publish to the repo GH package registry; action fails fast on missing telemetry adapter but can be configured to warn in non-blocking mode.

Commits (high-level): - commit 1: scaffold service + CLI entrypoint and schema docs - commit 2: implement telemetry presence matcher and risk model - commit 3: add staged runner with dry-run mode and trace format - commit 4: add GitHub Action + unit tests - commit 5: fix lint and type issues, add reviewer-requested telemetry adapter fallback

Files changed (high level): - services/playbook_scorer/* (core scoring logic, tests) - runner/staged_runner/* (executor, dry-run, undo registration) - bin/ib-playbook-score (CLI wrapper) - ci/playbook_score_check.yml (GitHub Action) - docs/playbook_schema.md (new schema and examples) - examples/sample_playbooks/* (two annotated example playbooks) - tests/integration/test_scoring_pipeline.py - README updates in incident-bot/README.md

Example usage: ib-playbook-score score examples/sample_playbooks/db_incident.yml --simulate-cost --output report.json; the report includes score breakdown: telemetry_coverage: 62, step_risk_median: 28, estimated_cost_seconds: 420, confidence: low.

Review conversation (condensed): - Arjun Patel (2026-02-11): "Nice direction. Two asks: 1) make the action undo annotation mandatory only for high-risk actions; 2) ensure the GH Action can be opt-out per repo via .github/config.yml". Author reply (Maya Chen 2026-02-12): "Implemented conditional enforcement (configurable threshold) and added repo opt-out config; updated docs and tests." - Lena Rodriguez (2026-02-13): "Can the runner operate in a sandboxed namespace for K8s actions? Concerned about accidental deletes." Author reply (Maya Chen 2026-02-14): "Added --sandbox flag and a K8s dry-run adapter that uses server-side dry run + mock apply to validate undo steps. See runner adapters." - Tomás Silva (2026-02-15): "CI initially failing lint and type checks; after fixes looks good. Please add a small metric for playbook_score_histogram to help product analyze distribution." Author reply (Maya Chen 2026-02-15): "Added playbook_score_histogram metric and dashboard stub in observability-pack/queries.md".

CI and checks: - Initial run: lint failed (flake8-coded style and a mypy issue) - After commit 5: all unit tests pass, integration tests for scorer run in ~40s on CI runner, lint and type checks pass - Final CI status: pass. Action run also validated the examples.

Backward compatibility and safety: This PR does not change runtime APIs used by incident-bot other than adding an optional telemetry adapter interface. Playbook schema extensions are additive and the GitHub Action is opt-out via repo config. Staged runner is opt-in: playbooks must include a new 'runner: staged' annotation to be executed by the staged runner. Undo steps are recommended for high-risk steps; enforcement is configurable.

Migration and rollout plan: - Soft launch: Add GH Action in warn-only mode for three internal infra repos for 2 weeks to gather score distribution. - Opt-in: recommended for teams building automated remediations; provide training doc and two example playbooks. - Block mode: enable enforce mode for critical infra repos once recommended score threshold is stabilized.

Testing performed: Unit tests for scoring heuristics (coverage and edge cases), integration test that runs scorer against synthetic telemetry datasets, manual validation of staged runner against a k8s test cluster (sandbox mode), and smoke tests for CLI.

Known limitations and follow-ups: - Current cost models are heuristic-based; follow-up work tracked in ENG-4590 to plug realtime execution metrics pipeline to refine estimates. - Telemetry adapter coverage must be improved for some legacy services; added a ticket SRE-1084 to onboard missing indices. - Will follow up with analytics dashboard to visualize playbook score trends and to correlate with incident MTTR (SRE-1070).

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main by Arjun Patel after approvals from all reviewers and final CI green. Changelog entry and release notes pushed to docs/releases/2026-02.md.
notes: CLI and GitHub Action added; internal rollout plan included in PR body. See ENG-4521 and SRE-1070 for followups.
